dedupe_keys.name: odym open dynamic material systems model

description: ODYM (Open Dynamic Material Systems Model) is an open-source Python framework for dynamic material flow analysis, that is, for modelling the stocks and flows of materials through society over time. Systems, processes, stocks, flows and parameters are described as objects, and any depth of detail can be traced at once: products, components, sub-components, materials, alloys, waste and chemical elements. It includes a library for dynamic stock modelling, in which product inflows and lifetime distributions determine in-use stocks and end-of-life outflows, the waste streams that collection, recycling and disposal infrastructure must handle. Stefan Pauliuk and Niko Heeren described it in the Journal of Industrial Ecology (published online 2019), and it is now maintained under the International Society for Industrial Ecology. Coverage is generic: any region, product system and time span the user defines; resolution follows the user's classification. Inputs and outputs use a standardised file format and data templates so that data can be exchanged between projects. It is Python source on GitHub, installed with pip, with documentation and six tutorials. Licence: MIT, free. Caveats: it is a framework, so users must build and parameterise their own system and gather data, and it does not represent the spatial layout of facilities. Simulation uses: projecting future waste and scrap flows for capacity planning of recycling and waste treatment infrastructure, and circular-economy and climate scenarios. Related: SwolfPy models the treatment side of municipal solid waste systems (catalogued as model-swolfpy).
